widgets_values: If your video has an audio channel you need, right now you must manually drag the audio output from Load Video node to the ref_video_audio_0 input on the top left of the workflow. nodes.title: Temporal Upsampling (De-Roping)
widgets_values:
This option detects areas of quick motion in your gen and duplicates the frames allowing the model to regenerate them correctly, removing the duplicated frames at the end. The result effectively cleans smudgy, blurry, lossy artifacts caused by distance and high velocity. It is recommended for any shots that aren't stationary dialogue scenes!

The amount of deroping steps is set to 1/2 of your main stage steps.

nodes.title: Custom Forced Audio
widgets_values: Custom Audio: if enabled, <Audio 1> will completely replace the gen's audio latent, forcing video to match what it hears -- great for lipsyncing dialogue shots in either T2V/I2V, or REF2VA! Just make sure the audio duration is close to the video gen duration, and that any dialogue is written clearly in <d>dialogue</d> tags in the prompt (improves lipsync).

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the character in <Picture 1>. (describe character attributes if needed)
<Subject 2> is the location in <Picture 2>. (describe location details)
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1>. (audio 1 should be 15 sec of a person talking)

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] A cinematic scene located in <Subject 2> of <Subject 1> speaking.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre guides the vocal delivery of <Subject 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1]: <Subject 1> is standing in front of the camera in <Subject 2> while staring out into the distance. She speaks the line of dialogue in <Audio 1>: <d>What's next, strap a leash on me? I'm not a pet cat, you weirdo!</d>. She has a flippant and sarcastic expression as she speaks. 
[Shot 2] at 00:05: A profile view medium shot of <Subject 1> as she turns towards the camera and walks off the frame.

overall_soundscape:
(Describe ambience, specific sounds to address)

widgets_values:
https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md

ref2va is EXTREMELY programmatic. Meaning, the instructions you give must be accurate for consistent results. Use the above guide to reference the instructional keywords/tags for use in your own prompts. You can be creative and use natural language for most situations.

Does it have to be as complicated? Not really. But according to the prompting guide, the model likes firm instructions like this.

nodes.title: Prompt
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the white hero car defined by reference image: a modern metallic-white performance sedan with a wide black horizontal grille, angular LED headlights, sculpted hood, clean aerodynamic bodywork, and realistic wet reflective paint. Preserve its exact exterior design, proportions, color, headlights, wheels, and body details throughout.
<Picture 2> is the driver defined by reference image: a serious light-skinned young adult man with short dark hair, angular facial features, clean-shaven face, and a fitted black leather jacket. He drives <Picture 1> with both hands firmly controlling the steering wheel, focused eyes, restrained facial movement, and natural posture.
<Picture 3> is the black pursuing car defined by reference image: a glossy black classic boxy European sports sedan with twin circular headlights, a narrow twin-kidney grille, amber corner lamps, black trim, and period-correct wheels. Preserve its exact identity, proportions, paint, lights, and details.
<Video 1> is the 15.64-second grey Blender previs My Video-2.mp4. It defines the complete shot duration, continuous camera choreography, framing, perspective, vehicle scale, road positions, relative spacing, movement, and timing.

summary: [video editing] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. Replace the unfinished grey Blender geometry with a photorealistic live-action nighttime car sequence. The large foreground vehicle becomes <Picture 1>, driven by <Picture 2>, while the smaller following vehicle becomes <Picture 3>. Preserve the original animation and uninterrupted camera path exactly.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (entire target video): fully_preserved - retain the original 15.64-second duration, single continuous shot, camera trajectory, framing progression, vehicle animation, spatial blocking, relative distance, and pacing.
<Picture 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - transfer the white car’s complete exterior identity onto the main foreground vehicle while preserving the source vehicle’s animation and screen position.
<Picture 2> (appears inside <Picture 1> in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - maintain the referenced face, hair, black leather jacket, serious expression, and driver identity whenever visible through the glass.
<Picture 3> (appears behind <Picture 1> in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - transfer the black classic sedan’s complete exterior identity onto the secondary vehicle while preserving its source movement and spacing.

detailed_description: The target video is a photorealistic live-action cinematic car sequence in the original 5:4 composition, filmed at night inside a long urban concrete underpass during heavy rain. Wet asphalt produces physically accurate reflections from headlights and overhead industrial lights. Concrete walls carry restrained weathering and distant graffiti. Use realistic vehicle suspension, tire contact, rain interaction, glass reflections, subtle body vibration, natural motion blur, shallow cinematic depth of field, high dynamic range, and cool blue-grey color grading with warm amber practical-light accents.

[Shot 1] Begin with the exact opening composition and scale of <Video 1>: an extremely close low side-profile tracking view of <Picture 1>, filling most of the frame as it travels through the tunnel. Preserve the original camera speed and distance. Rain beads and streams across the white bodywork and windows; the spinning wheels throw fine water spray from the road. <Picture 2> remains correctly seated behind the steering wheel, visible only when the original camera angle naturally reveals him through the side glass.

The camera executes the same uninterrupted slow Arc Shot from the broad side profile toward the front quarter of <Picture 1>, matching every change in perspective from <Video 1>. As the camera clears the front corner, reveal the white sedan’s angular illuminated headlights, black grille, wet sculpted hood, and realistic reflections. <Picture 3> becomes visible farther behind in the same lane and at the exact relative position established by the previs, following steadily without overtaking or changing the source choreography.

Continue the original frontal tracking composition through the ending. The camera remains stabilized and low while both cars maintain believable forward momentum. Keep <Picture 1> dominant in the foreground and <Picture 3> partially visible behind it. Preserve the source ending position and angle exactly. No cuts, collisions, drifting, invented maneuvers, geometry changes, extra vehicles, pedestrians, logos, captions, or text. Prevent vehicle morphing, wheel deformation, identity swapping, floating tires, sliding without wheel rotation, and inconsistent driver appearance.

overall_soundscape: Heavy rain strikes metal, glass, and pavement. The white sedan’s refined engine note, tire hiss, water spray, tunnel reverberation, and the deeper distant engine of the pursuing black sedan move naturally with their positions. No dialogue.

non_diegetic_music: A restrained cinematic electronic score with low pulsing synthesizer bass, sparse industrial percussion, and gradually rising tension. Keep the music beneath the engines and rain, building subtly toward the final frontal composition without a dramatic climax.
